scope: READ_ONLY incremental priority/applicability audit. Correctness NOT assessed. Only the four named local documents were inspected; prior SC/DGM literature work was reused, not repeated.
summary: No checked published theorem was established to cover RP-LIFT's exact order-preserving, R=p, all-odd-constant-reflection-block, one-rotation-pair statement. This is a bounded applicability finding, not evidence of novelty.

RP-LIFT's integer-increment lifting is elementary short-arc rectification plus connectivity [INFERENCE]. Rectification is already used explicitly in recent dihedral sequencing work, but under different hypotheses and for choosing an ordering.

The exact SIGN inequality was not matched to a checked source theorem. Its LIGHT component is routine cyclic averaging; the prescribed transition band and marked-weight bookkeeping remain the candidate-specific assembly.

The strongest incremental BASE2 finding is Lev's 2022 few-subsequence-sums theorem: it supplies the positive-coefficient, interval-subsum normal form for every core occurring in these two cell proofs, including the length-11 C_23 core below the usual half-group threshold [INFERENCE application of a checked theorem].

Complement symmetry and the subsequent interval intersections are elementary mechanisms, not an independent structural-theorem contribution. The complete two-cell LS statements were not identified as direct published corollaries.

RP-LIFT.candidate_exact: p≥5 prime; word length 4p−2 in D_(2p); exactly p rotation letters, all from {ρ_x,ρ_−x}, x≠0; every maximal cyclic constant reflection block has odd length; κ=p−1−Σ floor(l_i/2), with 1≤κ≤(p−3)/2. Conclusion: an identity-product subsequence of exactly 2p letters in increasing ORIGINAL index order. No restriction on reflection values or minority-rotation count B.

mechanisms.name: FWIN: parity-sensitive fixed half-cycle
mechanisms.exact_interface: For κ+1≤m(P)≤(p+1)/2, avoidance forces ψ(P)=−B+Σ_(i∈P)(e(θ_i)−d_i) into [1,p−1]⊂C_(2p).
mechanisms.comparison: The even lift is ordinary parity/CRT bookkeeping; turning the variable E(P)-window into this common interval is the lane-specific reduction. Neither Green–Ruzsa nor the checked dihedral rectification lemma states this reduction.
mechanisms.relation: Familiar algebraic ingredients; exact application not established as a source-theorem corollary.

mechanisms.name: CONNECT
mechanisms.exact_interface: Patterns on a k-cycle with exactly m cyclic intervals, adjacent by one-index toggles preserving m; connectivity required when 2m<k, including P↔P^c.
mechanisms.comparison: The 2m unlabelled boundaries move exactly as tokens on C_k. Token Graphs, Theorem 1, supplies connectivity for that unlabelled configuration graph. It does NOT automatically supply connectivity of the pattern graph: a boundary set represents both P and P^c, so the alternating-label/complement issue remains.
mechanisms.relation: Classical configuration-space analogue, not a verified direct import.

mechanisms.name: ILIFT
mechanisms.exact_interface: All pattern values have representatives N(P)∈[1,p−1]; same-coordinate edges differ modulo 2p by the same α_i. Obtain common integer increments h_i and layerwise constants c_m.
mechanisms.comparison: [INFERENCE] This is the elementary F_2 no-wrap principle. The interval diameter is p−2, and 2(p−2)<2p. Equal modular differences between its points therefore have equal integer differences. Connectivity then makes N(P)−Σ_(i∈P)h_i constant on each layer. No small-doubling theorem is needed.
mechanisms.qualification: Green–Ruzsa formulate their introductory observation for prime modulus. Its extension here to modulus 2p is the elementary inequality argument, not their stated prime-modulus theorem.
mechanisms.relation: Routine/corollary-level lifting ONCE FWIN and CONNECT are available.

mechanisms.name: LIGHT and SIGN
mechanisms.exact_interface: k=p+2κ nonzero integer weights h_i, with 2κ marked positions satisfying |h_i|≥2 and all others ≥1; seek signs with 2κ+2 through p+1 cyclic transitions and Σs_i h_i>p−2.
mechanisms.comparison: LIGHT is cyclic-translate averaging [INFERENCE]. Flipping light nonadjacent stretches or internal vertices is an elementary alteration method. No checked theorem supplied SIGN's simultaneous lower/upper transition constraint and strict weighted lower bound.
mechanisms.relation: Exact constrained lemma remains unmatched; neither novelty nor an existing-theorem equivalence is established.

closest_contrary_or_equivalent_results.statement: A solvable group of order n with a (2n−2)-multiset having no n-sum of result 1 must be cyclic, with exactly two values each repeated n−1 times.
closest_contrary_or_equivalent_results.comparison: At n=2p the length and selected cardinality match RP-LIFT. But the paper's input is an unordered multiset and an r-sum receives a designated ordering. It guarantees some ordering of the selected terms, not inherited index order. Thus it does not establish RP-LIFT, even though its group hypotheses are broader.

closest_contrary_or_equivalent_results.statement: For finite noncyclic G with 4∤|G|, E(G)≤3|G|/2, with equality exactly when G has a cyclic index-two subgroup.
closest_contrary_or_equivalent_results.comparison: Specializing gives E(D_(2p))=3p [INFERENCE]. Its definition explicitly permits multiplication in some order. The shorter numerical threshold cannot be substituted for an order-preserving theorem.

closest_contrary_or_equivalent_results.statement: Low-dissociative-dimension subsets of Z_p⋊H can be rectified into a short coordinate interval by an automorphism; their main theorem constructs sequencings of sufficiently small sets.
closest_contrary_or_equivalent_results.comparison: This establishes that rectification is already a tool in dihedral ordering research. It concerns sets, a low-dimension/small-set regime, and a chosen ordering with distinct partial products. RP-LIFT concerns repeated letters in a prescribed word and fixed-cardinality identity subsequences. No implication or contradiction follows.

exact_two_cell_claims.threshold_equivalent_form: For an all-odd multiset Y over C_34 with |Y|=42, exclusion of zero-sum subsequences of even lengths 26 through 34 implies there is no zero-sum subsequence of length ≥36.
exact_two_cell_claims.boundary: This is the candidate's RED-equivalent sequence formulation; not an ordered-dihedral conclusion.

exact_two_cell_claims.threshold_equivalent_form: For an all-odd multiset Y over C_46 with |Y|=56, exclusion of zero-sum subsequences of even lengths 34 through 46 implies there is no zero-sum subsequence of length ≥48.
exact_two_cell_claims.boundary: No LS+, STAB, or all-BASE2 result is claimed.

mechanisms.name: Complement symmetry and interval trapping
mechanisms.comparison: For A=Σ(U)∪{0}, A=σ(U)−A follows by taking complementary submultisets. This is the unrestricted-length version of the complement identity already checked in v3's DGM source. Intersecting an avoided interval with its reflected translate is elementary [INFERENCE].
mechanisms.exact_B2_step: If all nonempty sums of Y' lie in [1,B], and Z* has total 1, then every proper nonempty subsum x of Z* must satisfy x,1−x∈[1,B], hence x∈[p+1−B,B] [INFERENCE].
mechanisms.qualification: B can exceed p/2, so the raw trapping interval does not itself meet the short-arc F_2 no-wrap hypothesis.
mechanisms.relation: Routine identities and interval arithmetic; the later pair/triple and extension exclusions are not a quoted classification theorem.

mechanisms.name: Lev few-sums normal form
mechanisms.source_theorem_exact: For a zero-sum-free sequence α of length n in any abelian group, if its subsum set INCLUDING 0 has size <2n, then α=(x_1a,…,x_na), with 1=x_1≤…≤x_n, x_(j+1)≤x_1+…+x_j, and Σ(α)={0,a,…,Sa}, S=Σx_i<ord(a) when a has finite order.
applications: [INFERENCE] C_17 core in §3: |U'|∈{9,11}; residues 1,…,4 are absent, so |Σ(U')∪{0}|≤13<2|U'|. Lev supplies the normal form and full coefficient interval directly.
[INFERENCE] C_23 cores: |U'|=10+δ', 1≤δ'≤5. Residues 2,…,6 are absent, so the inclusive subsum set has size ≤18<22≤2|U'|. This includes δ'=1, |U'|=11<23/2.
[INFERENCE] In the δ'=1 C_23 branch, residues 1,…,6 are absent, improving the bound to 17<22.
[INFERENCE] B2-1's δ0=1 setting: |U|=2m+3 and residues 1,…,2m−2 are absent, giving inclusive subsum-set size ≤4m+1<4m+6=2|U|.
mechanisms.incremental_vs_v3: The generic SC half-group barrier is not an obstruction to normalizing THESE cores: their forbidden residues provide the stronger few-sums hypothesis. This does not contradict SC's sharp generic length threshold.
mechanisms.missing_for_complete_cells: Lev does not pin a=−1, control the removed Z0, or supply the long-zero-sum witness/non-extension contradiction. It is a structural input, not the complete LS theorem.
mechanisms.publication_status: Checked as public arXiv v3 and an author-hosted manuscript; journal publication was not established.

mechanisms.name: Published forbidden-length comparison
mechanisms.source_theorem_exact: disc_ℓ(C_n)=n+1 for n≥3 and 2≤ℓ≤n−1; disc_ℓ asks for a nonempty zero-sum whose length is NOT equal to one specified ℓ.
mechanisms.comparison: This does not force a zero-sum into BASE2's forbidden window. It may return an allowed short zero-sum. The paper's title is not evidence that it covers these cells.
mechanisms.relation: Different invariant; no direct implication established.

A consequential general result or new broad method is not established.
